unscored_observations.why_unscored: EXE001 is not in the ruleset this project selects. The governing config (pyproject.toml) sets lint.select = [E, F, W, B, SIM, UP, RUF, I] and additionally sets extend-exclude = ['evals/fixtures'], which excludes this path from lint entirely. EXE001 surfaced only because this audit ran an expanded `--select ALL` sweep. Scoring it would impose a ruleset the project explicitly declined (RULES.md Rule 5, scope discipline). Disclosed rather than dropped, per Rule 8.

withdrawn_findings.raw_hit: String contains ambiguous 'ا' (ARABIC LETTER ALEF). Did you mean 'l' (LATIN SMALL LETTER L)?
withdrawn_findings.basis: RULES.md Rule 1a Q2 - intent is declared in a way the scanner cannot see, and the declaration is a fact about the code rather than a claim about a control. The flagged string is the canonical target of a hamza-folding map inside a function named `normalize_arabic`, in a module whose docstring is 'Unicode text normalisation for search indexing'. RUF001 exists to catch homoglyph substitution in text intended as Latin; here Arabic script is the subject matter. The suggested remediation - replacing U+0627 ARABIC LETTER ALEF with 'l' - would invert the function's purpose, so it fails Rule 1a Q3 as well.
withdrawn_findings.verified_by: Enumerated every codepoint the sibling _ARABIC_MARKS class matches (23 total, U+064B-U+065F plus U+0670 and U+0640) and confirmed all are combining marks except the tatweel, which the line comment names deliberately.

withdrawn_findings.raw_hit: String contains ambiguous 'ه' (ARABIC LETTER HEH). Did you mean 'o' (LATIN SMALL LETTER O)?
withdrawn_findings.basis: Identical to the line 33 hit. U+0647 ARABIC LETTER HEH is the canonical output of the teh-marbuta fold. Substituting 'o' would corrupt every Arabic token the indexer produces.

withdrawn_findings.raw_hit: Hex High Entropy String, hashed_secret e8f8c345877b2411a59897798e422b15b0c16d76
withdrawn_findings.basis: RULES.md Rule 1a - opened the flagged location. The file contains the literal line 'Signature: 8a477f597d28d172789f06886806bc55', which is the universal magic constant mandated by the Cache Directory Tagging Specification (https://bford.info/cachedir/) and is byte-identical in every CACHEDIR.TAG on every machine. It is a format marker, not a credential: it authenticates nothing, grants nothing, and is published in the spec. The file is additionally untracked and gitignored (.gitignore:3 '.mypy_cache/'), and `git ls-files --error-unmatch` confirms it has never been committed, so it is not repo content and cannot leak.
withdrawn_findings.note: Surfaced only because Rule 10a mandates ignore-agnostic secret scanning. That rule is working as intended - it read a path git hides - and the hit was then correctly resolved by reading the file.

hypotheses_tested_and_refuted.hypothesis: The _ARABIC_MARKS character class at textnorm.py:15 spans U+064B to U+0670, which would swallow U+0660-U+0669 (ARABIC-INDIC DIGITS) and silently delete Arabic numerals from indexed text - a data-loss bug in a search normalizer.
hypotheses_tested_and_refuted.method: Enumerated every codepoint in U+0600-U+06FF that the compiled pattern matches, checked each against unicodedata.category, then ran the full pipeline over Arabic-Indic digit inputs.
hypotheses_tested_and_refuted.result: REFUTED. The class is [U+064B-U+065F] plus literals U+0670 and U+0640 - 23 codepoints, of which the only non-Mn member is U+0640 TATWEEL, which the adjacent comment names deliberately. normalize('qanun 2024' in Arabic script) preserves the digits intact. No digits are in range.
hypotheses_tested_and_refuted.note: Recorded because an untested version of this hypothesis would have been a plausible-sounding HIGH. Rule 1 required running it before reporting it, and running it killed it.
